title: Agentic Systems Architect
notes: Seeded from the verbatim Imagine Learning posting (the posting that motivated this role). This is a single, high-signal posting; the nightly research cycle should broaden to >=25 postings and recompute frequencies. Every requirement below is mapped to a curriculum module in curriculum-plan.json. See JOB_REQUIREMENTS.md for the readable traceability table.

postings.title: Agentic Systems Architect
postings.location: Remote - US (offices: Tempe AZ HQ, Austin TX, Petaluma CA, Rock Rapids IA, Bloomington MN)
postings.work_authorization: US Person required; sponsorship not available

summary: Owns the design, evolution, and governance of agent-based systems enabling autonomous and semi-autonomous workflows. The concrete charter is an internal AI-for-SDLC platform that extends an agentic coding tool (Claude Code) via a plugin architecture (Agents, Skills, Hooks, MCP), letting the AI securely interface with internal SDLC toolchains and proprietary data to perform requirements analysis, code generation, and debugging - security-first, governed, and compliant with FERPA/COPPA.

requirements.text: Design and evolve a plugin-based architecture (Agents, Skills, Hooks, Model Context Protocol/MCP) to extend Claude Code so AI can securely interface with internal SDLC toolchains and proprietary data.
Develop and optimize production AI applications via prompt engineering, context management, and tool-use patterns.

Develop reliable tool-use patterns and context-hydration strategies giving the agent precise system access/context to execute SDLC tasks (requirements analysis, code generation, debugging) autonomously.
Design AI systems compliant with data privacy / regulatory requirements including FERPA and COPPA in regulated EdTech environments.
Design developer-focused tooling emphasizing usability, adoption, onboarding, documentation, and continuous feedback loops.

Apply a security-first approach to local and remote agent execution: robust sandboxing, strict permission scopes, and secure authentication flows for CLI-based AI tools to prevent destructive actions or data leakage.
Drive the governance strategy for the AI SDLC platform: how plugins are evaluated, versioned, approved, and monitored to prevent unauthorized changes or quality degradation.
Lead estimation, scoping, and planning for AI/ML initiatives with executive and senior stakeholders; deliver strategic platform milestones within Agile/SDLC best practices.
requirements.note: Leadership/delivery competency primarily owned by the team-lead track (level 40); architect track frames it as platform-milestone scoping.

requirements.text: Lead continuous improvement across system architecture, engineering quality, and AI model integration via hands-on leadership and measurable outcomes.
8 years as Lead Software Engineer / Platform Architect / AI Engineering Lead (Bachelor's; or 6+ with Master's; or 5+ with PhD).
requirements.note: Prerequisite/experience gate, not a teachable module. Recorded in PREREQUISITES.md.

requirements.text: Proven experience building AI-enabled developer tooling, function-calling (tool-use) pipelines, or extensible agentic platforms in production; architecting modular, extensible, scalable platforms.
Proficiency in TypeScript/Node.js and/or Python; designing modular APIs, SDKs, or CLI tools; strong understanding of REST, GraphQL, and event-driven architectures.
requirements.note: Track examples provided in both TS/Node and Python.

requirements.text: Working knowledge of data privacy and compliance requirements in regulated environments, including FERPA and COPPA.
Deep understanding of secure system design: authentication flows (OAuth, token management for toolchains), RBAC, and mitigating AI vulnerabilities like insecure tool execution and prompt injection.
Intimate knowledge of the modern SDLC and integrating with core DevOps and project-management toolchains (GitHub, Confluence, Jira, CI/CD).
Familiarity with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ('a major plus').
Familiarity with RAG or embedding-based retrieval.
